rv.q: It all makes for an explosion of a show that feels surprisingly, joyously, fresh, a quarter of a century on.
East is East is an eruption of a show that forces us to consider it.
Iqbal Khan ’s production is electrifyingly dynamic and uproariously funny.

Ayub Khan-Din’s play about a Pakistani father trying to impose his traditionalist rules on his mixed-race children in the Salford of the 1970s remains full of serious insight into the meaning of multiculturalism.
That drawback, unfortunately, recurs – there does need to be better projection (or amplification) and enunciation.
It’s a fun, often very funny evening which will chime with battling kids and parents everywhere.
And so, to a lesser degree, does Iqbal Khan's current 25th-anniversary revival, presented in collaboration with Birmingham Rep.
Khan knows the right notes to hit to ensure it still works as well today, while also giving the production enough of its own flavour to make it worth revisiting.

cn.t: Critics largely praise this 25th anniversary revival as timely and uproariously funny, though some find it falls short of the original's impact. Iqbal Khan's dynamic production keeps Khan Din's culture-clash classic relevant.
